lines: A good tool is <pulse>quiet proof</pulse> that someone cared before trouble started.
I once fixed a pick that had seen more stone than sense.
A shovel broke on me once because I asked it to do axe work.
There is a story from the smithing table, but it sounds smaller unless you were standing there.
Once a hoe came back bent into a shape I still cannot explain.
A miner brought me a pick so worn it looked proud of itself.
I fixed an axe before sunrise and heard it saved two fences by noon.
A child asked for a tiny shovel and immediately became very official.
The first handle I made split because I thought confidence counted as grain sense.
During a storm, half the village arrived needing repairs and dry socks.
A trader tried to sell me my own repaired tool. Bold day.
I once found a missing chisel exactly where I had already looked loudly.
A shovel broke during a funeral for a fence post. Long story.
The grindstone once sang so badly everyone checked their teeth.
A cracked handle warned me before a bad swing could.
I repaired a fishing rod and learned fishermen blame everything but knots.
There was a week when every axe in town chose drama.
A golem watched me sharpen a tool and seemed personally invested.
The oldest hammer here has outlasted three benches and too many opinions.
